algorithm: beam search, width 2, branching factor 3 per beam member (6 experiments/round, 2 of which must tweak a regularization hyperparameter)
success_criterion: val_loss < 0.45 on any single epoch of a trial
noise_floor_note: User direction 2026-07-24: val_loss > 0.595 should be treated as noise, not a real result. Under this bar, every esm2_t6_8M-phase trial (0.596-0.6015 across 22 trials, rounds 1-2) was noise - none of that phase's beam-search 'winners' were ever distinguishable from the trial-015 seed. Only trial-030 (0.5946) and trial-031 (0.5918), both at esm2_t12_35M scale, have cleared 0.595 so far. Apply this bar to every trial ranking going forward.

final_beam.note: round-2 winner: weight_decay 0.5->0.2 off trial-018; ties trial-018 (0.5959) within noise, does not beat it
round-2 runner-up: unfreeze_last_n 1->2 off trial-018; ties trial-018 within noise, ~24% slower per epoch

esm2_t6_8M.paused_reason: Round 2's best result (trial-025, val_loss=0.5960) is statistically indistinguishable from round 1's best (trial-018, val_loss=0.5959) - the round-1 caveat's trigger condition ('if round 2 doesn't break the plateau meaningfully, raise with the user') was met. 12 trials across 2 rounds spanning all regularization and non-regularization axes moved best val_loss from 0.599 to 0.5959, essentially flat since round 1. Raised with the user 2026-07-24; user chose to pivot to model scale rather than continue tuning at this scale. This phase is paused, not abandoned - resumable if the 35M phase needs a same-scale comparison point.

history.note: ad hoc single-axis exploration, trial-001 through trial-017 (trial-017 abandoned after 3 infra failures)

history.what_helped: Both non-regularization schedule/optimization tweaks (cosine lr decay, larger effective batch via grad accumulation) gave small real reductions vs the trial-015 seed (0.599 -> 0.596/0.598). Every trial's best epoch landed at epoch 8/10, suggesting the plateau is being approached from above rather than a random walk.
history.what_hurt: Both regularization tweaks (label_smoothing, decouple_bias_wd) underperformed or merely tied the seed - no evidence we're currently overfitting hard enough for more regularization to help (train/val gap stayed a modest ~0.01-0.02 throughout). unfreeze_last_n=3 was worse AND noisier (val_loss oscillated 0.60-0.622 across epochs) AND ~48% slower per epoch (327s vs 220s) than unfreeze=1, for no benefit - more capacity alone is not the fix.
history.caveat: All 6 results (0.5959-0.6015) sit within a narrow band of the seed (0.599) and show meaningful epoch-to-epoch noise even within a single trial (e.g. trial-018 itself ranges 0.5959-0.6044 across its own 10 epochs) - round 1's 'winner' margin is close to that noise floor, so trial-018/trial-022 are the best available signal per the beam-search protocol, not confirmed robust wins. All results are far from the val_loss<0.45 target; nothing so far suggests wd/dropout/schedule tuning alone will close that gap at this model scale (esm2_t6_8M, unfreeze<=3) - worth watching whether round 2 breaks the plateau meaningfully before committing to more rounds at this scale.
history.bug_found: training_run.py computed train_acc/train_recall against the label-smoothed targets instead of the original hard 0/1 labels, so trial-020 (label_smoothing=0.05) reported train_acc=train_recall=0.0000 every epoch - an exact-equality-comparison artifact, not a real training failure (val metrics were unaffected since smoothing is train-only). Fixed post-hoc by computing metrics against a separate hard_labels tensor; val_loss numbers used for the round-1 ranking were never affected by this bug.
history.decision: beam updated to [trial-018, trial-022]; round 2 (trial-024..029) branches 3 children off each, 2 of 6 tweak regularization (weight_decay from trial-018, output_dropout from trial-022) - both in the 'reduce' direction given the under- vs over-regularization question raised above.

history.what_helped: Lower weight_decay (trial-025) and unfreeze=2 (trial-026), both off the trial-018 lineage, marginally edged past their parent's noise band - but neither beats trial-018's own best (0.5959) in absolute terms.
history.what_hurt: Stacking cosine schedule onto trial-022 (trial-027) did not combine round-1's two gains additively - worse than trial-018 alone, so the two round-1 wins weren't independent. grad_accum=4 (trial-029) was flat-to-worse than grad_accum=2. Lowering output_dropout further (trial-028) was the worst trial of the round.
history.plateau_confirmed: Round 2's best (trial-025, 0.5960) is statistically indistinguishable from round 1's best (trial-018, 0.5959) - a 0.0001 gap, an order of magnitude below single-trial epoch-to-epoch noise (~0.004-0.008). Best val_loss has been essentially flat since round 1 (0.599 -> 0.5959 -> 0.5960) despite covering every regularization and non-regularization axis in both directions across 12 trials. val_acc/val_recall also converge to near-identical values regardless of config. Reads as a representational/data-budget ceiling for esm2_t6_8M at max_train_samples=12000, not a remaining hyperparameter to find.
history.decision: Beam updated to [trial-025, trial-026] per protocol, but round 3 design paused - raising the plateau with the user before spending more Colab trials on this model scale, per the trigger condition logged after round 1.

esm2_t12_35M_scale_up.why: User-directed pivot after the esm2_t6_8M phase's round-1/round-2 plateau (best val_loss flat at ~0.596 across 12 trials, all far from the val_loss<0.45 target). Per the project's original plan, once a config is confirmed at small scale, scale up and re-run the regularization search from scratch rather than assuming settings transfer. esm2_t12_35M is the project's actual default model (SELECTED_MODEL in training_run.py) and was only ever tried once before, in trial-007, at 1 epoch pre-beam-search - not a fair comparison to the now-mature 10-epoch/tuned-baseline methodology.

fixed_across_all_rounds.note: User direction 2026-07-24: keep epochs fixed at 10 for every trial at this scale, model size aside, for cross-run comparability, and because harsh overfitting has been observed to show up in later epochs (trial-031's train/val gap was still widening at epoch 6, its last epoch). EXCEPTION: trial-030/031 (seed/diagnostic) and round_1 (trial-032..037) below were already launched at epochs=6 before this policy was set - their results are not directly epoch-for-epoch comparable to anything run at epochs=10, only their per-epoch trajectories (e.g. best_epoch, overfitting onset) are.

seed_config.note: Deliberately the esm2_t6_8M phase's actually-validated baseline (trial-015 through trial-029 all clustered around this), not the round-1/2 micro-tweaks (cosine schedule, wd=0.2, unfreeze=2) which never beat it outside noise - re-running 'from scratch' means not assuming those noise-level effects transfer either.

seed_results.verdict: MILD OVERFITTING - same shape as trial-031 (val_loss rises 0.5946->0.5959 after epoch 4 while train_loss keeps falling), just much weaker (train/val gap widens ~0 to only ~0.016, vs trial-031's ~0.03 to ~0.04). Clears the 0.595 noise floor, unlike every esm2_t6_8M-phase trial. ~530s/epoch (~2.3x slower than 8M scale).

OVERFITTING - best result of the whole sweep at epoch 4, but train_loss keeps falling (0.6012->0.5584) while val_loss rises after epoch 4 (0.5918->0.5988 by epoch 6); train/val gap widens from ~0.03 to ~0.04. First clear overfitting signal in the entire sweep (8M phase never showed this regardless of regularization level) - confirms regularization is a real, measurable lever at this scale, not just capacity.

round_1.status: in_progress (epochs=6, predates the epochs=10 policy above - user reports trial-032/033/034 done, trial-035/036/037 still running as of 2026-07-24)
round_1.run_mode: user-run manual browser Colab session (kept alive via a different technique than the CLI flow) - no colab session for the assistant to stop; user closes it themselves once the batch finishes
round_1.gpu_memory_observations: User reports trial-033 (batch_size=128, grad_accum_steps=1) almost OOM'd the T4; trial-034 (batch_size=128, grad_accum_steps=4, run immediately after) was surprisingly easier on memory. Per training_run.py (create_esm/DataLoader), grad_accum_steps does NOT reduce per-step batch size - the DataLoader batch_size is used as-is every micro-step, so trial-034 processes full batches of 128 exactly like trial-033; the code gives no mechanism for grad_accum alone to lower peak memory. Most likely explanation: CUDA's caching allocator already expanded its pool to fit batch=128 during trial-033, so trial-034 (running right after, same session) reused that already-grown pool instead of needing to allocate further - an artifact of run order within one session, not a real property of grad_accum_steps. Don't read 'higher grad_accum = lower memory' as a real effect without a controlled A/B (same batch size, accum vs no-accum, in fresh sessions on both sides).
